title: Practice schedules
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Practice schedules
card: long practice blocks with short or no rests. Fatigue can build up, so it suits simple skills and fit, motivated learners.
shorter practice blocks with rests or breaks between them. It suits complex or tiring skills and beginners, as rests allow recovery and thinking.
one skill is practised over and over before moving to the next, such as 20 free throws in a row. It helps beginners get the basic movement.
several skills are mixed in an unpredictable order, such as a free throw, then a pass, then a lay-up. It is harder at first but suits learners who are more advanced, as it builds skills for a game.
draft.remember: Massed or distributed is about rest. Blocked or random is about the order of skills.

a.q: Which practice schedule is a coach using when a netball squad repeats shooting 30 times, then moves to passing 30 times?
a.why: Each skill is repeated in a row before the next one starts, which is blocked practice. Massed and distributed describe how much rest is taken, not the order of the skills.
a.clue: Look at the order of the skills, not the rests.

b.q: Priya has played tennis for years and is already skilled at her serve and volley. Her coach wants her to be ready for the changing demands of a match. Which schedule suits her best?
opts: Random practice, mixing serves, volleys and returns
Blocked practice, repeating only serves for the session
Blocked practice, as she needs the basic movement first
Massed practice, as it is best for every advanced player
b.why: Priya is already skilled, so mixing skills in an unpredictable order prepares her for a match. Blocked practice suits beginners learning the basic movement, which is the tempting wrong answer because it sounds like focused work. Massed practice is about rests, not the order of skills.
b.clue: Match games mix skills in an unpredictable order.

b.best: Random practice, mixing serves, volleys and returns
